description: Attack the dense cuSOLVER floor (shapes 3/8/11 n=512 b640, worst 208ms) with batched spectral divide-and-conquer via the matrix sign function: Newton-Schulz iterate sign(A - sigma*I) to build an invariant-subspace projector, split each matrix into two smaller blocks, recurse until blocks reach the fast mega_eigh n<=200 base case, then stitch eigenvectors back. Entirely batched GEMM (tensor-core), spectrum-independent fixed cost, pure torch. Distinct mechanism from the tridiag cluster kernel.

sign-function spectral D&C for n=512 dense-even (shape 11). Scaled NS sign(A) -> +/- projectors -> oversized fixed-K=300 invariant-subspace bases (batched CholeskyQR) -> two reduced K=300 blocks on the fused megakernel -> membership rank-select of the n true eigenpairs -> 1 FP32 NS orthonormalization. Per-matrix residual-gated + cuSOLVER fallback. shape11 207.7->170.5ms (-18%); shapes 3/8 unchanged; 39/39 valid; check pass. nsys: 2x mega_eigh_med_split_k (block eigh) 29%, NS-sign tf32 gemm 11%, CQR trsm 6.5%, FP32 orth-gate/final-NS simt_sgemm ~9%.

Reduce sign Newton-Schulz iters 30->24 (membership rank-select tolerates a fuzzy sign; shape-11 eig ~3.5e-3, ~3.5x under gate). shape11 170.5->159.8ms; geomean 33891->33715us; 39/39 valid; check pass.

Cache Omega probe blocks (fixed generator, by (b,n,K,dev)) to stop re-drawing 0.8GB randoms/call; NS sign iters 24->20 (eig ~3.6e-3). shape11 159.8->124.4ms (vs parent 207.7ms, -40%); geomean 33715->33070us; shapes 3/8 unchanged; 39/39 valid; check pass.

Fuse NS via baddbmm (1.5X-0.5 X@X2 one kernel, kills ~17ms elementwise); unmaterialized projectors P+/- @ M via baddbmm; final-NS + orth-gate Gram moved FP32-SIMT->3xTF32; eigen gate reuses solver A@Q (order-gathered, no extra GEMM). shape11 124.4->115.1ms (parent 207.7, -45%); geomean 33070->32998us; shapes 3/8 within noise; 39/39 valid; check pass.

Stack both +/- reduced blocks into single (2b,n,K) CQR + (2b,K,K) megakernel eigh launches (2b CTAs fill 148 SMs better; ~9% on block eigh). A@U per b-block (no af repeat). shape11 115.1->109.5ms (parent 207.7, -47%); geomean 32998->32809us; shape5 noise-checked (188ms); 39/39 valid; check pass.

Measured subspace-basis CQR passes=1 REGRESSES: shape 11 304ms (1 pass leaves rank-deficient P+/-@Omega bases too far from orthonormal -> membership split degrades -> mass cuSOLVER fallback) vs passes=2 109.7ms. Kept passes=2 (load-bearing); exposed as documented knob. geomean 32753us (==trial 5, CQR=2); 39/39 valid; check pass.

Swept subspace width K=272/280/288/294/300. K=272 regresses (15.6% cuSOLVER fallback). K in [288,300] all ~110ms at benchmark level (block eigh is the wall; K doesn't move it). Kept K=300 (0 fallback + reseed headroom, equal speed). geomean 32751us; shape11 109.4ms (parent 207.7, -47%); 39/39 valid; check pass.

Final confirmation + profile of HEAD 4f7abed0 (K=300). geomean 32765us (parent 34343, -4.6%); shape11 109.4ms (parent 207.7, -47%); shapes 3/8 unchanged (own low-rank paths); 39/39 valid; check pass. nsys shape11: block eigh mega_eigh_med_split_k 38.5% (38.5ms in-kernel, the wall), NS-sign/probe tf32 gemm 14.5%, CQR trsm 9%, elementwise 5.8%. Block eigh in-kernel FP32-SIMT cost is the megakernel's floor (recursion loses, K in [288,300] flat).

BRANCH HEAD 4f7abed0f02b4c8f8311f6d64d53cabcf6deca60. Built batched spectral divide-and-conquer via the matrix sign function for the n=512 dense-even class (shape 11). RESULT: geomean 34343->32765us (-4.6%); shape 11 (worst on board) 207.7->109.4ms (-47%); shapes 3/8 UNCHANGED (81ms/93ms, kept on their faster low-rank paths); 39/39 valid, check pass; 'stream' absent. Pure torch, reuses the parent's megakernel for the base case (no nvcc). Pipeline: scaled Newton-Schulz sign(A) (A^2 power-iter scale, 20 iters) -> +/- projectors (never materialized; P+/-@M via baddbmm) -> oversized fixed-K=300 invariant-subspace bases via batched CholeskyQR (2 passes REQUIRED) -> BOTH K-blocks stacked into ONE (2b,K,K) fused-megakernel eigh -> MEMBERSHIP rank-select (||P+/-V||) of the n true eigenpairs (this is the key that makes a fixed-K oversample exact despite the per-matrix-variable +count 219-294) -> 1 final 3xTF32 NS orthonormalization -> Rayleigh L. Per-matrix residual-gated + cuSOLVER fallback; reseed-robust (5 seeds all route+pass, eig 3.5-5.4e-3, 0 mass fallback).

KEY FINDINGS FOR ROUTING: sign-DC is the win ONLY for the gapless dense-even shape 11 where cuSOLVER's D&C cannot deflate. Shapes 3 (decaying, PR55) and 8 (rankdef, PR163) already have FASTER dedicated low-rank paths (81/93ms) that spectrum-independent sign-DC (~110ms) cannot beat -- so the brief's 'shapes 3/8/11 move together' hypothesis is refuted by measurement: only 11 moves, and it moves a lot.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did not fully close: (1) The reduced-block eigh (mega_eigh_med_split_k, ~38ms in-kernel) is the WALL at 38.5% of shape 11 -- it's the megakernel's own FP32-SIMT Householder+bisection+twisted cost at K=300, not tunable from my torch code. A follow-up could give the sign-DC blocks a dedicated block solver with a TF32/tf32x3 back-transform (the blocks are well-conditioned dense ~256-eigenvalue blocks, unlike the ill-conditioned low-rank reduced blocks), or a tensor-core batched tridiagonalization, to break this floor. (2) RECURSION (300-block -> 2x150 fast-kernel) was MEASURED to LOSE (53ms vs 29ms direct) -- the 2nd-level sign+CQR overhead exceeds the faster-leaf savings, same failure mode the codebase notes for brief-7 t7. (3) K in [288,300] is FLAT at the benchmark level (block eigh dominates); K=272 regresses (15.6% fallback). (4) CQR passes=1 REGRESSES hard (304ms, mass fallback) -- 2 is load-bearing for the rank-deficient projected bases. (5) NS iters 20 holds a ~3.4x eig margin; could probe 16-18 but diminishing. (6) The ~30ms of 'misc' small-kernel + Python-dispatch overhead per shape-11 call (109ms total vs ~85ms in named kernels) suggests a fused/CUDA-graph capture of the torch-level pipeline could recover more -- unexplored. (7) The sign(A) is currently applied to the FULL n=512 twice per iter (X@X, X@X2); a Denman-Beavers or Pade sign variant might converge the near-zero eigenvalues in fewer GEMMs. RECOMMEND the manager consider this HEAD as a stacking candidate (it touches only the shape-11 routing gap, orthogonal to shapes 3/8/9/12) and, for a follow-up brief, the dedicated-block-solver direction (1) as the way to push shape 11 below ~100ms.

Lever #2 SURGICAL: (a) replaced the stage-1 tridiag tree reductions (s2/vp/amax/Gershgorin, each ~10 __syncthreads at nt=1024, ~18 of ~20 barriers/column) with warp-shuffle block reductions _medsum/_medmin/_medmax (2 barriers each) -> kernel 38.5->34ms, shape11 109->104ms, and ALL med_split callers won (t10). STILL OPEN -- THE remaining lever: ncu after my changes shows the kernel is STILL 72.8% barrier-stalled (34ms). Stages 2/3 (bisection, twisted eigenvectors) are barrier-free (parallel over eigenvalues); ALL the stall is stage-1 tridiag's ~7 remaining per-column barriers (2 from each of the two _medsum + symv + p-update + rank-2-update). The structural fix is PANELIZED (blocked-WY / LAPACK latrd) tridiagonalization: accumulate PANW reflectors into V/W panels and do ONE rank-2*PANW trailing update per panel instead of one per column -- removes the trailing-update barriers (n -> n/PANW). SMEM fits (K=300 packed 90KB + W-panel n*16*4=19KB << 228KB; k=384 197KB). I did NOT attempt it: it's a ~150-line rewrite of a kernel SHARED by 5 shapes (2/3/8/11/12) with real correctness/SMEM-overflow risk, and I judged rushing it at end-of-budget would gamble the banked -50%. RECOMMEND a dedicated brief for the panelized tridiag (est. kernel 34->~25ms, shape11 104->~95ms). Other smaller openings: the CQR trsm is 9.5% of shape 11 (2-pass required, measured); the lingering FP32 simt_sgemm (2.9ms) is the sign-DC block back-transform kept at fp32 (tf32 fell back); ~fusing the torch-level pipeline (CUDA graph) could recover Python/dispatch overhead. Also note: this shape-11 gain is orthogonal to shapes 3/8/9/12's own paths, so the whole submission.py is a clean stacking base.

BUILT + measured lever #2 PANELIZATION (blocked-WY/latrd tridiag) in mega_eigh_med_split_k: accumulate panw reflectors into V/W SMEM panels, apply ONE rank-2*panw deferred trailing update per panel. Threaded panw through the cpp decl + host launcher (SMEM-clamped PW: k=384 caps ~24, K<=300 fits 32) + both callers. VALIDATED 39/39 correct (the math is right). But MEASURED 3-5x SLOWER: PANW=32 geomean 49890us (vs 32182), shape11 349ms (vs 104), shape2 33ms (vs 6), shape3 281ms, shape8 149ms. ROOT CAUSE: the deferred update needs the symv's low-rank corrections wtv[l]/vtv[l] = sum_j W/V[j][l]*v[j] for l<kk -- 2*kk block reductions per column (up to ~62 barriers/column at panw=32), which cost FAR more than the per-column trailing-update barrier they remove. ncu's 72.8% barrier stall is DIVERGENCE-before-barriers (triangular-update load imbalance), not barrier COUNT, so batching the update doesn't help and the corrections add barriers. REVERTED to e23884fa (proven global best, re-confirmed geomean 32138us, shape11 104ms, 39/39). Also measured: a 1-barrier warp-reduction variant = null (32266us), and a flat-triangular-index balanced update = regressed (sqrt-per-entry recovery too costly, 32818us).

PANELIZATION resume: HEAD stays e23884fa (proven global best; geomean 32138us re-confirmed, shape11 104ms, 39/39 valid, check pass, 'stream' absent). I BUILT the requested lever #2 (blocked-WY/latrd panelized tridiag) fully -- V/W SMEM panels, deferred rank-2*panw trailing update, panw threaded through cpp decl + host launcher (SMEM-clamped: k=384 caps ~24, K<=300 fits 32) + both callers -- and it VALIDATED 39/39 (math correct). But it MEASURED 3-5x SLOWER (PANW=32: geomean 49890us, shape11 349ms, shape2 33ms, shape3 281ms, shape8 149ms), so I reverted it to keep the branch HEAD at the global best you are submitting (I did NOT commit the regression as HEAD -- that would clobber the best; the full result is captured in the trial log).

WHY PANELIZATION LOSES HERE (measured, not conjectured): the deferred trailing update saves the per-column rank-2 update barrier (n -> n/panw), BUT the panel column factorization then needs the symv's low-rank corrections wtv[l]=sum_j W[j][l]v[j], vtv[l]=sum_j V[j][l]v[j] for l<kk -- 2*kk block reductions PER COLUMN (up to ~62 barriers/column at panw=32). Those cost far more than the single trailing-update barrier they remove. Crucially, ncu's 72.8% barrier stall is DIVERGENCE-BEFORE-BARRIERS (the triangular rank-2 update's per-row load imbalance: thread i does i-c writes), NOT barrier COUNT -- so batching the update into fewer-but-larger ops does not address the actual stall, and the corrections make it worse. This is a fundamental mismatch between blocked-WY (which wins on GPUs by turning the trailing update into a tensor-core GEMM) and this SINGLE-CTA SIMT-SMEM packed-FP16 kernel (no tensor cores in-CTA; the update is already SMEM-resident, so blocking only adds reduction overhead).

ALSO MEASURED this resume (both reverted): (a) 1-barrier warp-reduction variant of _medsum/min/max = NULL (32266us vs 32182; the removed barrier was a cheap broadcast, not the divergence-driven stall). (b) flat-triangular-index balanced rank-2 update (to fix the imbalance ncu flagged) = REGRESSED (32818us; the sqrt+while-loop (i,j)-recovery per entry costs more than the imbalance it removes).

WHAT REMAINS OPEN for the block-eigh wall (all point AWAY from in-CTA restructuring): (1) The real fix for the divergence stall is a CHEAP balanced triangular-update index map (avoid the per-entry sqrt -- e.g. a precomputed per-thread (i,j) start via a closed-form or a coarse 2D tiling), which I did not crack. (2) A genuinely DIFFERENT block solver that puts the O(k^3) work on TENSOR CORES: e.g. run the reduced-block eigh via a batched tensor-core tridiagonalization (SBR/successive band reduction) or route the well-conditioned blocks through a cuSOLVER batched path that fills the GPU -- the megakernel's single-CTA SIMT design is the ceiling, and no in-kernel tweak escapes it. (3) Outside the block eigh: the sign-side NS/probe GEMMs (14.8%) and CQR trsm (9.5%) are the next-largest shape-11 costs; a CUDA-graph capture of the torch-level sign-DC pipeline could recover the ~30ms Python/dispatch overhead (109ms total vs ~85ms in named kernels). RECOMMEND: treat the tensor-core block solver (2) as a separate macro brief; the barrier stall is not reducible by restructuring this SIMT kernel (three built+measured attempts confirm it). Net for brief-43 overall: shape 11 207.7->104ms (-50%), geomean 34343->32138 (-6.4%), all via the warp-shuffle reductions + fused reflector build (t10/t11) which stuck; the deeper block-eigh rewrite does not pay off in this kernel family.
